provides: LLM facade: JSON completion, translation, transcription and summarization in front of swappable model / speech-to-text / image-generation providers (Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, Claude Code CLI, whisper-http, ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI, openai-images), with a prompt cache and a per-call token ledger. Python port of a prior NestJS service — same HTTP paths/contracts, plus an in-process comm surface for monolith deployments.

curated.summary: LLM provider used when a completion request names none, resolved against the merged PROVIDERS registry (conf.py, MODULE.md 'LLM providers').
Speech-to-text provider used when a transcription request pins none and no language route matches (conf.py, MODULE.md).
Image-generation provider used when a request pins none, resolved against the merged IMAGE_PROVIDERS registry (conf.py, MODULE.md).
Per-source cache-by-prompt policy; the default answers from the latest matching success row within CACHE_TTL (conf.py, MODULE.md Settings table).

extension_points.name: PROVIDERS
extension_points.summary: Flagship seam: MERGE over providers.BUILTIN_PROVIDERS (anthropic/openai-compat/claude-code); None/'' removes a name; also extendable at runtime via register_provider(name, cls_or_path). ABC contract: complete()/resolve_model()/supports_images (MODULE.md 'LLM providers — open registry').

extension_points.name: STT_PROVIDERS
extension_points.summary: MERGE over stt.BUILTIN_STT_PROVIDERS (whisper-http/elevenlabs/assemblyai); same merge semantics as PROVIDERS (conf.py, MODULE.md Settings table).

extension_points.name: IMAGE_PROVIDERS
extension_points.summary: MERGE over images.BUILTIN_IMAGE_PROVIDERS (openai-images); same merge semantics as PROVIDERS (conf.py, MODULE.md Settings table).

extension_points.name: CACHE_POLICY
extension_points.summary: Dotted path to a CachePolicy subclass, in import_strings, instantiated per call (conf.py, MODULE.md 'Cache policy').

surface.name: detect_pwned_markers
surface.intent: The FLAG half of the flag/escape split: report which known prompt-injection markers a piece of untrusted text carries, without deciding any encoding. Run it on every LLM output and every retrieved chunk before that text reaches a consumer; the SafetyReport is what a caller branches on.

surface.name: detect_structured_output_leak
surface.intent: Run on any plain-text model answer before a consumer stores or renders it: returns the names of structured-output scaffolds (tool-call envelopes, parameter tags, chat-template tokens, schema echoes) that leaked into prose. The schema-constrained path proves its shape by construction and needs no canary; the prose path has no such proof, so this is the detector that says the answer is degraded and the text is markup nobody asked for (audit AI-01).

surface.name: redact_markers
surface.intent: The ESCAPE half for auto-escaping template engines (Jinja2): strips injection markers and does NO entity encoding, because the template engine already encodes and pre-encoding here double-escapes. Use this — not a hand-rolled replace — for any text rendered into a template.

surface.name: sanitize_for_rag
surface.intent: The ESCAPE half for text fed BACK into a model: strips markers and collapses whitespace. Mandatory for every retrieval chunk — an unfiltered marker inside a RAG chunk lands in the follow-up model's context and re-triggers the same attack, so 'the reader already flagged it' is not a reason to skip this.

surface.name: redaction_gate
surface.intent: Call before writing ANY model-produced text to a durable artifact (prompt log, cache row, transcript, report): raises RedactionError when the payload carries a provider key or the value of a *_API_KEY/_SECRET/_PASSWORD env var. It is a gate, not a filter — there is nothing to inspect afterwards, so an import without a call is the whole failure mode (that is exactly how it was lost once during a port: the import survived, the call did not).

requires.reason: the only stapel-* dependency: AppSettings, comm bus for in-process calls (pyproject.toml dependency)
